data.reason: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link down/up cycles: the WAN NIC transmit queue is wedged, so pings to the ISP gateway fail with ENOBUFS and its ARP entry is incomplete even though the interface reports active. The watchdog already performed 4 WAN reloads during this outage (12 in 24h, at its cap) with rc=0 each time and no recovery, so a further wan_reload will not clear the stuck driver queue; only a full reset of the host/NIC will. The cable modem itself reports OPERATIONAL/registered since 02:28, so a modem reboot would not help.

data.cause: The WAN interface's virtio driver transmit queue is stuck (repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" in dmesg), so packets cannot leave the firewall even though the link is up and the lease is valid; WAN reloads succeed but cannot unstick the queue, and the outage was originally triggered by an ISP-side cable-modem de-registration (T3 timeout / modem reboot at 02:28).
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP' cycles on the WAN NIC

ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 (ISP gateway): 100% loss with 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available', while netstat -m shows only 2306/3524 clusters in use and 0 mbuf denials — a stalled queue, not memory exhaustion
arp -a -n: entry for the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 is '(incomplete)' — no ARP reply from beyond the stuck NIC path, though the LAN host 10.20.0.9 resolves fine (local services still work)
ifconfig vtnet0: interface UP, RUNNING, LOWER_UP, status active with address 198.51.100.27; netstat -rn shows default via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 — config and lease look correct

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json: outage_start ~02:06, 4 reloads during this outage; events.jsonl shows each reload rc=0 with no recovery, and at 03:30 the watchdog stopped acting ('reload_cap', 12 of max 12 reloads in 24h) after 5040s down

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: modem log 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44 and 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21; modem-metrics.jsonl then reports cm_status OPERATIONAL with good SNR (~37.7 dB) — the provider link recovered on its side while the firewall stayed down
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (firewall_reboot was requested; the maintainer could not be reached and the harness's conditions for acting without approval held, so it ran). A full reset re-initializes the wedged vtnet0 queue, which repeated DHCP/WAN reloads (all rc=0, now at the 12-per-24h cap) cannot do. After boot, verify the WAN pings the ISP gateway and that ARP resolves; if the same watchdog timeouts recur after reboot, suspect the virtio backend/host hardware and also have the ISP check the segment that caused the 02:01 T3 timeout.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN NIC transmit queue wedged (driver watchdog timeouts)
